epics.title: Skill Library and Skill Contracts
epics.description: Keep foundation skills as the shared base every project can select and none can edit. Give each project a library for skills it writes. Move only the MaxView incident skill into MaxView's library. Let authors pick from both groups without scanning one long list. This is Playbooks Part 3.
successMetrics: A published Playbook that names a foundation skill keeps today's file check, and that file is not copied into the store.
MaxView can select the incident skill as its own, and other projects are not offered it as a base skill.
An author can find a skill by name when both groups contain many skills.
An interactive agent task does not resume until the assignee approves a valid result.

items.title: Store immutable skill versions and pin them at publish
items.description: Add the skill version store for project skills and their companion files. Do not copy foundation skills into it. Parse skill frontmatter as YAML, copy type and kind to columns, and hash the project skill version plus its instruction files. Publish of a project skill freezes that version. A run of that policy checks the bundle hash. A run that names a foundation skill checks today's single-file hash and is never rehashed. Reference files stay out of the hash. A new publish names a foundation skill or a project skill version.
technicalDependencies: Playbook publish and the current agent-run policy
The background agent worker that checks the skill hash
nonFunctionalRequirements: Saving a version and resolving it at publish stays within 2 seconds at P95
Two saves cannot overwrite a stored version
definitionOfDone: A published Playbook that names a foundation skill still checks that file. The file is not copied into the store.
A published Playbook that names a project skill keeps its pinned bytes after the project skill is edited.
An instruction-file change on a project skill is not visible to a published Playbook until that Playbook is republished.
A project skill whose name matches a foundation skill is refused.
A node with a kind is checked against the loose result first and the kind second. A node with no kind keeps today's loose check.

items.title: Move the MaxView incident skill into the MaxView project
items.description: Copy only the MaxView incident investigation skill, including its guide and catalog, into MaxView's project skill library. Remove it from the shared foundation list. Do not copy any other existing skill. A published MaxView Playbook that still names one of the three old incident paths resolves to that project skill. Other projects are not offered it as a base skill. Point the recommender at the project skill for MaxView only, and remove only the worker's old-name shell check. Carry the project's reader client ID on the run specification. The worker has no fallback identity.
nonFunctionalRequirements: A source file over 200,000 bytes is skipped, logged, and does not create a version
definitionOfDone: MaxView can select the incident skill under This project.
Other projects do not see it under Base skills.
A published MaxView Playbook whose frozen path is one of the three old incident paths still resolves to the moved skill.
No other existing skill file is copied into the store.
The SkillOpt plan is renumbered to Part 4 in its own doc edit.
An incident run in a project with no reader identity fails with a clear message instead of using another project's identity.

items.title: Enforce library permissions and reference-file rules
items.description: Add the view and reference-approval permissions, and start checking the existing manage permission. Review who already holds that permission, globally and per project. A project role overrides a global role. The library menu appears only where Playbooks are enabled. Reference-file contents require author or approver permission. Generate and save reject capabilities, a reference-file key, invalid YAML, an unknown kind, and invalid decision labels. Names are unique in the project and cannot match a foundation skill name. A project skill whose file name matches a foundation skill is rejected. A project cannot edit a foundation skill.
technicalDependencies: The existing role and menu-visibility checks
nonFunctionalRequirements: A library list returns within 2 seconds at P95
Reference-file contents are omitted from view-only responses

items.title: Run interactive turns under the published policy
items.description: Register the interactive step as leaving Apex, with the same read-only profile refusal as a background agent step. Give it a frozen policy and a hash check. Each turn runs as a Playbook agent run on the step's thread and is admitted and spend-checked on its own. The step counts once toward the agent-step cap. The deadline matches the interview step. The assignee is notified when the step opens and 24 hours before it expires. Cancelling the run aborts an in-flight turn and closes the thread without deleting it. A triggered Playbook cannot be published when this step has no assignee.
technicalDependencies: The Playbook step registry and the approval-gate check
The existing chat session hook used by other agent surfaces
nonFunctionalRequirements: No agent run is in flight while the step waits for the assignee
A denied turn does not consume a hidden retry
definitionOfDone: A read-only interactive step needs no approval gate. A write profile is refused.
A proposal that fails either schema is retried out of view at most twice, then the assignee is told and can keep chatting.
Reaching the turn limit forces one proposal. After one rejected revision, the assignee can only approve or cancel.
When the deadline passes, the step expires and the run ends with no partial result.
The assignee is notified in the app and in Teams, and the notification opens the run.

implementationPhases.rationale: There is one epic. FEAT-001 keeps foundation skills as shared files, stores project skills, moves the MaxView incident skill, and groups the skill control. FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 depend on that store and can proceed after it exists. They do not depend on each other.

assumptionsMade: The accepted ADR "Playbooks Part 3: Skill Library and Skill Contracts" is the scope. This PRD does not add decisions.
Playbooks menu visibility stays the way a project turns Playbooks on. The library does not need its own flag.
MaxView already has a reader identity. Part 3 records it and does not create identities.
Existing foundation skills stay files. Only the MaxView incident skill is copied into a project library. Published Playbooks that name any other current skill path keep today's file check.
Each interactive turn runs as a Playbook agent run on the step's thread, not through the Agent Home chat path.
A Playbook author sees skill names, types, and kinds in the builder without the skill-view permission.
